title: Emrys and the Choir
premise: In the smoke-choked city of Vellamark, where magic was outlawed after the Sundering, Ivo Whitlock survives by hiding her gift for speaking with beasts behind a trade in harmless charms. When the old gods stir and begin answering prayers again, their returning power tears at the fraying covenant that keeps the wild realms from spilling into the mortal world — and every god wants a beast-speaker to broker their claims. Hunted by the Inquisition and manipulated by gods with rival agendas, Ivo discovers the covenant was broken deliberately by the god of silence, who feeds on unspoken prayers. To reforge it, she must surrender the one thing she has guarded for fifteen years — her own true name and the identity she built to survive — and in the final rite she gives up her voice to the beasts forever, becoming the bridge between realms rather than a woman standing apart from them.
about_author: Silas Zhou is the pen name of a former field linguist who spent a decade recording oral traditions in remote mountain villages before turning to fantasy. They write about gifts that cannot be put down and gods who listen too closely.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hour
chapters.summary: Ivo Whitlock sells a love charm to a grieving widow, quietly bargaining with the widow's cat for the truth of the husband's death. POV: Ivo. Establishes her double life, her rules for hiding her gift, and the fear that governs her. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking exhaustion.

chapters.title: What the Rats Knew First
chapters.summary: The rats of Vellamark stop speaking — then begin screaming one word: coming. POV: Ivo, with a brief interlude from an Inquisitorial clerk. Ivo realizes the beasts are hearing something beneath the city. Emotional beat: dread arriving through small, ordinary mouths.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered in Ash
chapters.summary: The shrine of the Hearthmother burns a supplicant's prayer into living flame for the first time in fifteen years, and the crowd riots. Ivo is caught in the crush and hears, unmistakably, a god say her name. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the past reaching out to claim her.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor with Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Dara Voss interrogates Ivo about the riot, courteous and terrible, revealing she has a list of suspected magic-bearers — and Ivo's name is on it. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the hunter's patience as a form of violence.

chapters.title: The Stag in the Cistern
chapters.summary: A god in the shape of a drowned stag corners Ivo beneath the city and demands she speak for it in the courts of the returning pantheon. It offers protection; it also reveals her mother made a bargain Ivo never knew about. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: inheritance as a trap.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Small Charms
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter: young Ivo's first betrayal, when a childhood friend sold her secret and her family paid for it. POV: Ivo. Explains her rules, her fear of names, and why she never speaks her own aloud. Emotional beat: grief calcified into survival.

chapters.title: The Choir Assembles
chapters.summary: The old gods summon all mortal speakers to the ruined Cathedral of Whispers. Ivo arrives among a dozen hidden gift-bearers and hears them called the Choir — the covenant's intended voice. POV: Ivo, introducing rival speaker Tam Ossler. Emotional beat: terrified belonging.

chapters.title: Rules of the Broken Covenant
chapters.summary: The god of thresholds explains the Sundering: the covenant bound gods to answer only honest prayers, and someone taught mortals to lie to heaven. POV: Ivo. The Choir learns the covenant can be reforged — at a price none of them can yet name. Emotional beat: hope with a hidden invoice.

chapters.title: Tam's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tam Ossler, a weather-speaker, secretly offers the god of storms the Choir's loyalty in exchange for his brother's life, fracturing the group before it begins. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: love justifying treachery.

chapters.title: The Silence That Eats Prayers
chapters.summary: Ivo investigates vanished prayers and finds the hollow god — the one who broke the covenant — wearing the face of her dead mother in a dream. It does not threaten her; it offers her rest. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: temptation shaped like mercy.

chapters.title: Voss Closes In
chapters.summary: Dara Voss arrests two Choir members and offers Ivo freedom in exchange for naming the others. Ivo lies to a god's face to protect them, and the lie costs a piece of her gift. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the price of loyalty made physical.

chapters.title: The Market of Small Gods
chapters.summary: Ivo descends into the black market where minor spirits sell favors, seeking a way to restore what the lie cost her. She trades a memory of her mother's real face. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: erosion — survival spending the self it protects.

chapters.title: What the Beasts Call Her
chapters.summary: The animals of Vellamark reveal they have always known Ivo's true name and have kept it for her — a revelation that both wounds and steadies her. POV: Ivo, with the crows' chorus. Emotional beat: being known at last, and surviving it.

chapters.title: The Rite at Greyford Bridge
chapters.summary: The Choir attempts the first reforging at the threshold god's bridge; Tam's secret bargain sabotages it, and the backlash kills one of their own. POV: Tam, then Ivo. Emotional beat: grief and fury fusing into resolve.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Firelight
chapters.summary: Voss confronts Ivo with evidence of the failed rite — but instead of arresting her, she confesses her own buried gift and her fear of it. An uneasy alliance forms. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: enemies discovering shared cages.

chapters.title: The Hollow God's History
chapters.summary: The stag-god shows Ivo the truth: the hollow god was once the covenant's keeper, driven mad by fifteen years of unanswered prayers, and Ivo's mother helped break the seal to free it. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: compassion for the monster, horror at the lineage.

chapters.title: Every Prayer at Once
chapters.summary: The hollow god unleashes the hoarded prayers of fifteen years on Vellamark; the city drowns in answered wishes gone wrong. Ivo and Voss fight through a miracle-flooded streetscape to reach the Choir. POV: alternating Ivo and Voss. Emotional beat: awe weaponized.

chapters.title: Tam's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Tam confesses his betrayal to the Choir and offers his gift as payment; the storm-god takes it, and Tam is left ordinary and grieving but honest. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: the cost of repair — you cannot unmake, only pay.

chapters.title: The Name in the Deep
chapters.summary: Ivo descends to the covenant's root beneath the cathedral, where the hollow god waits wearing every face she has ever lost. It offers her the ending she always wanted: to stop being Ivo Whitlock. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the temptation of self-annihilation.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: The climax: Ivo accepts — but on her terms. She speaks her true name into the covenant, giving up her human voice to the beasts forever, and reforges the bond so gods must hear honest prayer and mortals must speak honestly to be heard. The hollow god, finally answered, dissolves into quiet. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: transcendence through surrender.

chapters.title: After the Choir
chapters.summary: The city reckons with a world where magic is legal and prayers are binding; Voss dismantles her own Inquisition from within. Ivo, voiceless among humans, is fluent among beasts, and finds a strange peace. POV: Voss, then Ivo. Emotional beat: bittersweet new order.

chapters.title: The Bridge Between
chapters.summary: A year later, Ivo serves as the covenant's living bridge, mediating between realms from Greyford Bridge. A child with a hidden gift comes to her, frightened, and Ivo — speaking through the crows — tells her she will not have to hide. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the price paid becomes a door held open for someone else.
